topics.topic: How agent requests through cabinet_kernel are authenticated, authorized, transported, and attributed across the trust boundary
questions: Under which principal and credential does the agent act, and what actor provenance must authorization and audit record?
What is cabinet_kernel relative to the portal, and how does a request passing through it reach the HTTP API while satisfying session transport, origin, host, authorization, and audit rules?

Is the cabinet_kernel sentence normative product behavior, and if so, whose credential or session authenticates the agent's requests, where is that trust boundary, and which actor is recorded in audit?
What is cabinet_kernel, where is its trust boundary, how does the agent receive or exercise the owner's session, and which principal and actor provenance are recorded for its requests?

quotes:
Client Portal IAM supports exactly three principal types. They are never
merged into one account model.

Every operation on a project's records — budget, snapshot, expense, document,
progress, payment and photo — checks together: valid active session (for a
service principal, its authenticated bearer credential of R0-09, which needs
no separate session), active principal, access to the concrete `project_id`,
required capability, and Registry project lifecycle policy (R0-15).

Every significant action records actor provenance: principal (`user_id`,
viewer, or service principal with credential/key version), `project_id`,
action, time, result, and affected business entity.

The owner decided on 2026-11-07: "remove the staff email/password challenge
feature from the spec. There are no human staff; the owner opens portal
sessions himself and an agent works through cabinet_kernel; no e-mails are
ever needed."
judgement.divergence: One implementation lets cabinet_kernel present the owner's StaffAccount session, authorizes the request as the owner, and audits only the owner's `user_id`; another treats the agent or cabinet_kernel as an unnamed principal or trust boundary with no valid credential and refuses the request. The owner, caller, and audit reviewer notice the difference.
judgement.why: The new text names an agent and cabinet_kernel as participants but does not assign them one of the three principal types, a credential path, a trust-boundary role, failure behavior, or audit provenance.

witness.initial: The owner has an active administrator StaffAccount, a valid staff session, and an active project containing an expense.
events: The agent asks cabinet_kernel to correct the expense allocation.
cabinet_kernel sends or forwards the correction request to the portal.
outcomes: The portal accepts the owner's staff-session credential, performs the correction, and records the owner's `user_id` as the actor.
The portal refuses the request because neither the agent nor cabinet_kernel has a defined portal principal and credential.
witness.observer: The owner and an administrator reviewing the audit trail
basis:
The owner decided on 2026-11-07: "remove the staff email/password challenge
feature from the spec. There are no human staff; the owner opens portal
sessions himself and an agent works through cabinet_kernel; no e-mails are
ever needed."

For an active project an operator can: correct, include, or exclude an
expense; allocate or manually split it across sections or `Other expenses`
(allocation sum equals the expense total; automatic proportional split is
forbidden); update manual work progress per section (0–100%); register work
payments (idempotent by stable payment identity); publish progress photos and
manage caption, section association, and visibility; maintain the manual
budget; review and activate imported budget versions.

Every significant action records actor provenance: principal (`user_id`,
viewer, or service principal with credential/key version), `project_id`,
action, time, result, and affected business entity.

topics.topic: Whether StaffAccount retains a verification fact and what recovery override verification means or affects
questions: Does a staff account still contain a verification status or fact, and if so, what does it mean when no verification operation exists?
Does StaffAccount retain any email-verification fact after email verification was removed, and precisely what state does "marks it verified" change during a recovery override?
Does a staff account still contain an email-verification fact, and if so what action, authorization decision, output or invariant observes it now that authentication depends only on active status?

quotes:
The portal therefore has no email verification, no email change
confirmed at a new address, no password reset, no security notification and
no email delivery, and sends no email to any address. A staff account's email
is its login identifier only.

The exceptional recovery override is an administrator action that replaces a
staff account's login email with a given address, marks it verified, and is
audited as `staff.recovery_override` atomically with the change; it is the
one operation that changes a login email, and an exceptional one (accepted
contract `perform_recovery_override`).
judgement.divergence: One passage requires email to be only a login identifier with no email-verification fact; the other requires recovery override to mark the replacement email verified. A domain or persistence implementer and a caller receiving the changed account observe whether verification state exists and changes.
judgement.why: The removal says email has no verification meaning beyond identifying login, while the recovery operation still explicitly produces a verified state.

The portal therefore has no email verification, no email change
confirmed at a new address, no password reset, no security notification and
no email delivery, and sends no email to any address. A staff account's email
is its login identifier only.

The exceptional recovery override is an administrator action that replaces a
staff account's login email with a given address, marks it verified, and is
audited as `staff.recovery_override` atomically with the change; it is the
one operation that changes a login email, and an exceptional one (accepted
contract `perform_recovery_override`).

witness.initial: An active StaffAccount has an existing login email.
events: An administrator performs the exceptional recovery override with a replacement email.
The portal commits the account change and returns or persists the changed account state.
outcomes: Only the login identifier changes because the account has no email-verification fact.
The login identifier changes and the replacement address is marked verified.
witness.observer: The administrator receiving the result and the persistence implementer
basis:
The exceptional recovery override is an administrator action that replaces a
staff account's login email with a given address, marks it verified, and is
audited as `staff.recovery_override` atomically with the change; it is the
one operation that changes a login email, and an exceptional one (accepted
contract `perform_recovery_override`).

Administrators additionally hold access-management capabilities (users,
assignments, client viewers, viewer grants and access links, service
principals, revocation) within their administrative area (R0-14).

topics.topic: Whether human StaffAccount actors remain and who may perform human-reserved staff actions
questions: Are human StaffAccount actors still part of the required product workflow, or are owner-operated agent actions intended to replace every human-staff action, including actions explicitly reserved to a human?

Are the owner and account holder human StaffAccount principals despite the statement that there are no human staff, and which actor is permitted to perform actions reserved for a human operator or administrator?

quotes:
The owner decided on 2026-11-07: "remove the staff email/password challenge
feature from the spec. There are no human staff; the owner opens portal
sessions himself and an agent works through cabinet_kernel; no e-mails are
ever needed."

The administrator then activates the account (`pending_verification` →
`active`); the holder logs in with the initial password and changes it
(accepted contracts `create_staff_account`, `change_staff_status`,
`change_staff_password`). No email is sent and no challenge is confirmed on
the way (R0-23).
judgement.divergence: One implementation treats possession of the owner's authenticated StaffAccount session as sufficient and permits the agent through cabinet_kernel to activate a snapshot; another enforces the stated human-review reservation and refuses agent-performed activation until the owner personally acts. The owner, producer, client, and audit reviewer notice which budget becomes active and who is treated as actor.
judgement.why: The texts require human performance for activation while also saying there are no human staff and that an agent works through cabinet_kernel, without deciding whether the agent may perform human-reserved actions under the owner's session.

witness.initial: An approved estimate snapshot has been imported for an active project and awaits review and activation; the owner has an active administrator session.
events: The owner opens the portal session.
An agent working through cabinet_kernel requests activation of the imported version.
outcomes: The portal accepts the request under the owner's StaffAccount session and activates the version.
The portal refuses or withholds activation because the requesting agent is not the human operator or administrator required to review and activate it.
witness.observer: The owner, the client reading the active budget, and the audit reviewer
basis:
The owner decided on 2026-11-07: "remove the staff email/password challenge
feature from the spec. There are no human staff; the owner opens portal
sessions himself and an agent works through cabinet_kernel; no e-mails are
ever needed."

For an active project an operator can: correct, include, or exclude an
expense; allocate or manually split it across sections or `Other expenses`
(allocation sum equals the expense total; automatic proportional split is
forbidden); update manual work progress per section (0–100%); register work
payments (idempotent by stable payment identity); publish progress photos and
manage caption, section association, and visibility; maintain the manual
budget; review and activate imported budget versions.

topics.topic: How a newly issued or re-issued ViewerAccessCredential is returned to the client without portal messaging
questions: What observable output returns a newly issued or re-issued capability link, and which named actor or external boundary conveys it to the client without portal messaging?

quotes:
`ViewerCredentialIssue`: the new `ViewerAccessCredential` and the secret in
plaintext, returned once.
None: the owner passes the code to the client outside the portal.
judgement.why: The later public operation returns the plaintext secret once to the administrator-side caller and explicitly assigns the owner the out-of-band handoff to the client.

topics.topic: How staff access is recovered after password loss when the login email remains known
questions: What action, if any, restores access when a staff account loses its password but its login email is still known, especially for the sole administrator?

quotes:
The exceptional recovery override is an administrator action that replaces a
staff account's login email with a given address, marks it verified, and is
audited as `staff.recovery_override` atomically with the change; it is the
one operation that changes a login email, and an exceptional one (accepted
contract `perform_recovery_override`). No product operation recovers a sole administrator who has lost both password
and email: the bootstrap command of R0-07 refuses once any staff account
exists, and such a recovery stays a host-level operation outside the product
(owner 2026-11-06: current service behaviour accepted; technical decisions
delegated).
The portal has no email-challenge or password-reset operation (R0-23).
judgement.divergence: One implementation leaves a sole administrator whose password is lost permanently unable to regain product access even when the login email is known; another supplies a host-level password recovery action by extending the stated host recovery boundary beyond the case where both password and email are lost. The owner operating the deployment notices the difference.
judgement.why: The texts remove password reset and define the recovery override as email replacement, but specify host recovery only for loss of both email and password, leaving password-only loss undecided.

witness.initial: The deployment has exactly one active administrator; the owner knows its login email but has lost its password.
events: The owner attempts staff login and fails.
The owner cannot invoke an authenticated administrator recovery override.
The owner runs or considers the bootstrap command, which refuses because a staff account already exists.
outcomes: No specified action restores access, so the deployment remains inaccessible through the product and documented host command.
A host-level recovery action resets or replaces the lost password and restores administrator access.
basis: The portal has no email-challenge or password-reset operation (R0-23).

The exceptional recovery override is an administrator action that replaces a
staff account's login email with a given address, marks it verified, and is
audited as `staff.recovery_override` atomically with the change; it is the
one operation that changes a login email, and an exceptional one (accepted
contract `perform_recovery_override`). No product operation recovers a sole administrator who has lost both password
and email: the bootstrap command of R0-07 refuses once any staff account
exists, and such a recovery stays a host-level operation outside the product
(owner 2026-11-06: current service behaviour accepted; technical decisions
delegated).

An empty deployment cannot acquire its first operator through the API, because
creating a staff account needs an authorized administrator. The host operator
runs a local administrative command that creates exactly one active
administrator when no staff account exists, and is refused once any exists.
